html:
A hydroelectric dam on the Volta River in Ghana, built from 1961 to 1965. It created Lake Volta, the largest reservoir in the world by surface area.

It was the dream of Kwame Nkrumah, who saw cheap power as the base for industry in newly independent Ghana. The project was paid for by Ghana with loans from the World Bank, Britain and the United States. Its main customer was an aluminium smelter at Tema, run by the American firm Kaiser Aluminum, which bought the power cheaply.

The lake flooded a vast area and forced about 80,000 people from hundreds of towns and villages to move. The still water spread bilharzia, a disease carried by snails. Nkrumah opened the dam in January 1966; a month later he was overthrown in a coup. The dam still produces much of Ghana's electricity, and the lake carries boats and supports fisheries. It is often compared with the Kariba Dam on the Zambezi.
sum: A hydroelectric dam on the Volta River in Ghana, built from 1961 to 1965. It created Lake Volta, the largest reservoir in the world by surface area.
